items.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Shenny Walker. I was trying to think of him. I used to go around to his house to jam sessions.

ctx.x: There’s also information here about Memphis. I’ll read it into the record. These are your words, so we’ll let it speak for itself. Once returned to Ole Miss, you took weekend trips to Memphis. In ‘47 and ‘48, you went to various clubs. You met Phineas Newborn, Jr. You met Don Brooks, a white alto player in the city. And you met B.B. King’s bass player, Shenny Walker.
Yeah, Shenny Walker. I was trying to think of him. I used to go around to his house to jam sessions.

Patti Jones writes: “Walker provided an important entree into the black music world, sneaking Mose into the black clubs on the chitlin circuit and passing the white Allison off as his ‘cousin’ when necessary.”
